A team is validating a generative AI assistant for an organization. The assistant generates responses using internal knowledge sources.  
  
The organization requires assurance that responses are accurate, source-supported, and relevant to user prompts before production access is enabled.  
  
You need to implement quality metrics that verify the assistant produces dependable and meaningful responses.  
  
Which two evaluation metrics should you use? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation: Groundedness evaluates whether generated content is supported by the supplied knowledge sources, helping verify factual, source-backed responses. Relevance evaluates whether the response addresses the user’s prompt. Together, these metrics measure the required source support and prompt alignment.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) solution produces incomplete answers because relevant content is retrieved inconsistently from the knowledge source.  
  
You need to increase RAG accuracy without changing the embedding model that is currently used. You must meet this goal while minimizing operational costs.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution. Choose two.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Tune chunk size and overlap to match content structure.
Increase token limits for all requests.
Optimize the length of embedding vectors.

questions.explanation:
Chunking content at an appropriate size with overlap preserves semantic context across chunk boundaries and improves the likelihood that relevant passages are retrieved. A reranker performs a second relevance evaluation of retrieved candidates against the query, improving the ordering and selection of context provided to the RAG model. Microsoft Learn recommends tuning chunk size and overlap for vector-search relevance and describes reranking as a way to evaluate candidate documents that initial vector or keyword searches might otherwise rank inaccurately.

**Learn more:** [Vector Relevance and Ranking - Azure AI Search](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/vector-search-ranking) · [Develop a RAG Solution—Information-Retrieval Phase](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/ai-ml/guide/rag/rag-information-retrieval)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A product team is creating a customer-support assistant that must provide consistent responses through multiple channels.  
  
Early tests reveal that minor wording differences in prompts lead to major changes in tone and factual accuracy.  
  
The team requires prompts that are dependable, reusable, and adaptable for multiple use cases without retraining the underlying model.  
  
You need to create prompts that improve response quality while preserving flexibility for future changes.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution. (Choose two.)  
  
NOTE: Each correct choice is worth one point.

options.text: Fine-tune the model for each conversational variation.
Apply prompt transformations to separate system instructions from user input.
Use the system prompt to establish the role, tone, and style.
Increase the temperature setting to encourage creativity.
Repeat the instructions at the end of the system prompt.

questions.explanation:
System prompts provide persistent, high-priority guidance for an assistant’s role, tone, style, and behavioral constraints. Separating those trusted system instructions from user-supplied input creates clear instruction boundaries, making prompts safer to reuse and easier to adapt across use cases without changing or retraining the model. Higher temperature increases output variability, and fine-tuning each variation is neither necessary nor flexible for this requirement.

**Learn more:** [System message design for Azure OpenAI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/advanced-prompt-engineering?view=foundry-classic) · [Prompt engineering in .NET](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/ai/conceptual/prompt-engineering-dotnet)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You train machine learning models in Azure Machine Learning and use Hyperdrive to tune hyperparameters.  
  
In earlier model-training and tuning runs, many models delivered similar performance.  
  
You need to choose an early-termination policy that meets these requirements:  
  
- accounts for the performance of all prior runs when assessing the current run  
- does not compare the current run only with the best-performing run so far  
  
Which two early-termination policies should you use? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Median stopping computes running averages across all training runs and terminates a run when its primary metric is worse than the median of those averages. Truncation selection compares runs by their primary metric and cancels a specified percentage of the lowest-performing runs at each evaluation interval. Both evaluate performance relative to the group of runs, whereas Bandit policy uses the most successful run as its reference.

**Learn more:** [Hyperparameter tuning a model (v1) - Azure Machine Learning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/how-to-tune-hyperparameters?view=azureml-api-1) · [MedianStoppingPolicy class - Azure Machine Learning Python](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/python/api/azureml-train-core/azureml.train.hyperdrive.medianstoppingpolicy?view=azure-ml-py)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have created a workspace by using Azure Machine Learning Studio.

You need to reset the notebook’s state.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has several data science teams working on distinct machine learning projects.  
  
The company requires models to be auditable, reusable, and centrally governed across teams. The models must support team-level isolation for billing.  
  
You need to set up the foundation for governed machine learning operations.  
  
Which action should you take first?

options.text: Register shared datasets in a central storage account.
Create a shared hub workspace and project workspaces for each team.
Create a resource group for shared machine learning assets.
Create a shared Azure Machine Learning workspace.

questions.explanation:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A financial services company is deploying Microsoft Foundry to host generative AI workloads that handle regulated customer data. The Microsoft Foundry environment must eliminate public network exposure while continuing to allow Microsoft Foundry-managed services to communicate with dependent Azure resources.  
  
Security auditors require all traffic to and from the Microsoft Foundry resource to stay on private networks, with no public endpoints available.  
  
You need to configure the Microsoft Foundry environment to restrict network access while preserving full platform functionality.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution. Choose two.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Configure a managed virtual network for the Microsoft Foundry resource.
Use API key authentication for all model endpoints.
Deploy the Microsoft Foundry resource in a separate Azure subscription.
Disable public network access to the Microsoft Foundry resource.

questions.explanation:
A managed virtual network provides an isolated network boundary for Microsoft Foundry-managed services and supports managed private endpoints to dependent Azure resources. Disabling public network access removes public exposure; access can instead occur through private endpoints. Authentication method and subscription placement do not establish private network isolation, and blocking all inbound access would not provide the necessary private-endpoint connectivity.

Both environments must use the same validated assets without duplicating those assets. Assets must be shared across workspaces while preserving centralized governance and version control.  
  
You need to enable asset reuse across workspaces without copying the assets.  
  
What should you do?

Publish the asset as a pipeline component.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A team deploys a model to a real-time endpoint in Azure Machine Learning and then deploys updates to that endpoint.  
  
The endpoint begins returning errors after the new deployment is released. You need to restore the service as quickly as possible.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Roll back traffic to the previous deployment.
Delete the endpoint and immediately redeploy it.
Change the authentication type to Azure Machine Learning token-based authentication.

Solution: `python train.py --training_data training_data`  
  
Does this solution fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Machine Learning command jobs reference a declared input in the command by using `${{inputs.training_data}}`, which resolves to the input data path at runtime. Passing `training_data` without that expression supplies a literal string rather than the dataset path; the command also does not invoke the identified `script.py` file.\
\
**Learn more:** [CLI (v2) command job YAML schema - Azure Machine Learning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/reference-yaml-job-command?view=azureml-api-2) · [Train ML models - Azure Machine Learning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/how-to-train-model?view=azureml-api-2)

Solution: `python script.py --trainingdata $\{\{inputs.training_data\}\}`  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation: A Python script that reads the `training_data` argument must receive the matching `--training_data` command-line parameter. Using `--trainingdata` omits the underscore and therefore does not provide the expected argument.

Proposed solution: `python script.py dataset1.csv`  
  
Does this solution satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Machine Learning command-job inputs are passed to a script by referencing the input path in the command and supplying the script’s named parameter, such as `python script.py --training_data ${{inputs.training_data}}`. A positional `dataset1.csv` value does not populate an argument named `training_data`.\
\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization is deploying several generative AI workloads using Microsoft Foundry. Each workload must satisfy distinct requirements for data governance, task specialization, and operational cost control.  
  
The organization requires models that meet the following requirements:  
  
- Model behavior aligns with the task being performed.  
- Data handling aligns with internal governance policies.  
- Operational complexity and cost are justified by workload needs.  
  
You need to select the foundation model options that meet the requirements.  
  
Which three models can you select? Each correct answer presents a complete solution. Choose three.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: A model that is optimized for conversational reasoning when deploying an interactive assistant
The largest available model to simplify operational management
The smallest available model to minimize the usage cost
A model that supports multiple input types when workloads require combined text and image analysis
A model that offers enterprise governance controls when workloads process regulated business data

questions.explanation:
Appropriate foundation-model selection matches the model to the workload’s required capability, supported modalities, compliance requirements, and cost/performance trade-offs. Conversational reasoning is appropriate for an interactive assistant, multimodal input support is required for text-and-image analysis, and enterprise governance controls are appropriate for regulated business data. Choosing the largest or smallest model solely on size does not ensure task fit, compliant data handling, or a justified operational trade-off.

Background

Fabrikam Inc. is a mid-sized healthcare analytics company that delivers population health dashboards and predictive insights to regional hospital systems across the United States. Fabrikam Inc. customers depend on near real-time analytics to monitor patient flow, staffing needs, and readmission risks. They use multiple traditional forecasting machine learning models for predictions.

Fabrikam Inc. has an established Microsoft Azure footprint. The company uses Jupyter Notebooks running on a local server as the main development environment. The data science team is experiencing scalability, asset management, and code management issues with the current development platform. Fabrikam Inc. plans to move to a cloud-based development environment to reduce these issues.

In addition, the company plans to implement a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based chat application for client support. Leadership requires the application to be developed and deployed with low operational risk.

Current Environment

Fabrikam Inc. operates a single Azure subscription that includes the following components:

- Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 that contains de-identified clinical and operational datasets
- Azure AI Search indexing curated analytical documents and reference materials
- A small set of Python-based training scripts maintained by data scientists
- Azure OpenAI Service with deployed foundational models
- A Microsoft Foundry resource for building a RAG-based solution
- Evaluation data with manually defined expected responses

The current challenges faced by the data science team include the following:

- Model training jobs are run manually from notebooks.
- Experiment tracking is inconsistent.
- Model versions are registered without standardized metadata.
- Deployment is performed manually by data scientists, with limited rollback capability.
- The team has no standardized evaluation process for generative AI outputs.
- The environment currently allows public network access.
- Authentication relies on user accounts rather than managed identities.
- Compute targets are manually created and shared across experiments. This has led to resource contention during peak usage.

Business Requirements

Fabrikam Inc. has the following business requirements for the modernization initiative:

- Provide a conversational interface that answers analytics questions by using internal documents and datasets.
- Ensure that sensitive healthcare-related data is not exposed outside the Fabrikam Inc. Azure tenant.
- Enable repeatable and auditable model training and deployment processes.
- Support experimentation to compare prompt strategies and fine-tuned models.
- Align the model with the ranked preferences and optimize behavior for the long term.
- Minimize disruption to existing analytics workloads during rollout.

Technical Requirements

To support the business goals, Fabrikam Inc. identifies these technical requirements:

- Use Azure Machine Learning workspaces to centrally manage data assets, models, and environments.
- Implement experiment tracking and model versioning for all training jobs.
- Orchestrate training and evaluation by using pipelines rather than manually running notebooks.
- Deploy traditional machine learning models with support for staged rollout and rollback.
- Improve RAG-based solution output quality.
- Use the existing evaluation datasets that are based on real data with input-output pairs.
- Apply advanced fine-tuning techniques only when prompt engineering is insufficient.

Issues and Constraints

Fabrikam Inc. must comply with internal security policies that require the company to restrict network access and avoid long-lived secrets. The data science team has limited Azure DevOps experience, so solutions must favor managed services and automation over custom infrastructure. Cost predictability is important. Leadership prefers serverless or managed compute options where possible but is willing to approve dedicated compute for stable production workloads.

Problem Statement

Fabrikam Inc. must design and implement an Azure-based AI operations solution that enables reliable training, evaluation, deployment, and iteration of generative AI models. The solution must support experimentation and gradual rollout while ensuring governance, security, and operational stability. A company’s platform engineers administer the resource settings and governance for Microsoft Foundry.  
  
Developers must be able to create and update project assets, but they must not be able to modify resource-level configurations.  
  
You need to enforce least-privilege access for the engineers and developers. Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution. Choose two.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Assign a resource-level Azure AI Administrator role to the platform engineers.
Disable Microsoft Entra ID authentication for the Microsoft Foundry resource.
Assign the Azure AI Developer role to the developers.
Share a single API key across all teams.

questions.explanation:
The Azure AI Administrator role provides control-plane permissions to manage Azure AI resources and their dependencies, which supports resource-level settings and governance. The Azure AI Developer role permits actions within an Azure AI resource but does not allow management of the resource itself, enabling developers to work with project assets without changing resource-level configuration. Microsoft Entra ID authentication supports granular Azure RBAC; disabling it or sharing API keys would undermine least-privilege access control.

**Learn more:** [Azure built-in roles - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You run Azure Machine Learning training experiments. The training scripts directory contains 100 files, including a file named `.amlignore`. The directory also contains subdirectories named `./outputs` and `./logs`.  
  
Twenty files in the training scripts directory must be excluded from the snapshot sent to the compute targets. You create a file named `.gitignore` in the root of the directory and add the names of the 20 files to it. The 20 files continue to be copied to the compute targets.  
  
You need to exclude the 20 files.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Move the file named .gitignore to the ./logs directory.
Move the file named .gitignore to the ./outputs directory.
Add the contents of the file named .amlignore to the file named .gitignore.
Copy the contents of the file named .gitignore to the file named .amlignore.

questions.explanation:
When both `.amlignore` and `.gitignore` exist in an Azure Machine Learning training-script directory, Azure Machine Learning uses `.amlignore` and ignores `.gitignore` for the source snapshot. `.amlignore` uses the same ignore-pattern syntax, so it must contain the 20 file patterns.

**Learn more:** [Configure a training job - Azure Machine Learning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/how-to-set-up-training-targets?view=azureml-api-1)

The model must provide low-latency predictions and automatically scale according to incoming request volume.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage an Azure Machine Learning workspace and build a model for which you need to configure a Responsible AI dashboard.  
  
Based on insights from the dashboard, you must perform these activities:  
  
- Determine the actions needed to obtain a desirable outcome from the model.  
- Identify the features with the most direct effect on the outcome of interest.  
  
You need to choose the components to use in the Responsible AI dashboard configuration.  
  
Which two components should you add? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
The counterfactuals component produces examples of the minimum feature changes that would lead to a desired prediction, helping determine what actions can achieve a desirable model outcome. The causal component estimates the effect of features on an outcome of interest and identifies features with the most direct effect.

**Learn more:** [Counterfactuals analysis and what-if - Azure Machine Learning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/concept-counterfactual-analysis?view=azureml-api-2) · [Make data-driven policies and influence decision-making - Azure Machine Learning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/concept-causal-inference?view=azureml-api-2)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A data science team intends to automatically evaluate multiple hyperparameter values while training a model in Azure Machine Learning.  
  
The tuning process must execute multiple training trials without manually changing the training script for every run.  
  
You need to automate hyperparameter tuning for the training job.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Manually change hyperparameter values between training runs.
Create a tuning job that runs multiple trials with different parameter values.
Duplicate the training script for each parameter combination.

questions.explanation:
An Azure Machine Learning tuning (sweep) job defines a hyperparameter search space and runs multiple trial jobs with different parameter values. This automates the evaluation of training configurations without manually altering or duplicating the training script for each trial.

**Learn more:** [Hyperparameter tuning a model (v2) - Azure Machine Learning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/how-to-tune-hyperparameters?view=azureml-api-2)

You create a workspace using Azure Machine Learning Studio.  
  
You must run a Python SDK v2 notebook in that workspace through Azure Machine Learning Studio. For the current instance, you must retain the present values of variables set in the notebook.  
  
You need to preserve the notebook state.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
Stopping the current kernel stops running cells without changing the notebook state or the values of variables. In contrast, changing the kernel or compute resets notebook state and variables, and stopping compute prevents cells from running.\
\
**Learn more:** [Run Jupyter notebooks in your workspace - Azure Machine Learning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/how-to-run-jupyter-notebooks?view=azureml-api-2)

questions.explanation:

An organization operates a customer-facing generative AI application built using Microsoft Foundry. The application uses multiple prompts connected to multiple workflows to generate production responses.  
  
The application occasionally produces incomplete responses. Although the model call succeeds, the final message sometimes ends early.  
  
The issue cannot be reproduced consistently in development.  
  
You need to determine where and why response generation is ending early in production.  
  
Which approach should you use?

options.text: Run a pre-release evaluation workflow to score groundedness and relevance on a test dataset.
Enable tracing and logging so that each workflow can be inspected.
Increase max_tokens and temperature to reduce the chance of early termination.
Replace the deployed model with a smaller model to reduce variability across responses.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Foundry tracing and logging capture request-level telemetry across agent and workflow execution, including model inputs and outputs, intermediate operations, timing, token usage, and errors. Inspecting these production traces identifies the workflow or operation at which the final response is truncated and supplies the context needed to determine why it terminated. [Set up tracing in Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/observability/how-to/trace-agent-setup)

**Learn more:** [Set up tracing in Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/observability/how-to/trace-agent-setup) · [Tracing and data handling — Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/observability/concepts/trace-data)

You create an Azure Machine Learning workspace.  
  
You must use the Python SDK v2 to implement an experiment from a Jupyter notebook in the workspace. The experiment must record a list of numerical metrics.  
  
You need to implement a method that logs a list of numerical metrics.  
  
Which method should you use?
questions.explanation:
`mlflow.log_batch()` logs multiple metric records in a single operation. `mlflow.log_metric()` is for one metric value, whereas artifact and image methods log non-metric data.\
\

The notebook is in an Azure Machine Learning workspace. It uses a training script that runs on a compute cluster with 20 nodes.  
  
The code implements a Bandit termination policy with `slackjactor` set to `0.2` and a sweep job with `max_concurrent_trials` set to `10`.  
  
You must increase the effectiveness of the tuning process by improving sampling convergence.  
  
You need to choose which sampling convergence setting to use.  
  
What should you select?

options.text: Set the value of max_concurrent_trials to 20.
Set the value of slack_factor of early_termination policy to 0.9.
Set the value of max_concurrent_trials to 4.
Set the value of slack_factor of early_termination policy to 0.1.

questions.explanation:
Bayesian sampling uses results from completed trials to choose promising later configurations. Limiting the number of concurrently running trials allows more completed-trial feedback to inform each new configuration, improving convergence. The Bandit policy’s slack factor controls how aggressively underperforming trials are terminated; it does not improve Bayesian sampling convergence.

**Learn more:** [Azure Machine Learning sweep job: Bayesian sampling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/how-to-tune-hyperparameters?view=azureml-api-2#bayesian-sampling)

Solution: Examine user-feedback comments gathered after deployment to determine whether answers seem more accurate.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Post-deployment feedback comments are subjective and do not directly measure whether generated claims are supported by the retrieved documents. A groundedness evaluator provides a measurable assessment of whether a RAG response aligns with its retrieved context and avoids fabricated content.\
\
**Learn more:** [Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Evaluators for Generative AI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/evaluation-evaluators/rag-evaluators)

Solution: Compare the embedding vector dimensions used by the retrieval pipeline before and after the change.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Embedding-vector dimensionality is a retrieval-pipeline configuration, not a measure of whether generated content is supported by retrieved documents. Groundedness evaluation measures whether a generated response aligns with the provided context without fabricating information, which directly addresses unsupported RAG answers.\
\
**Learn more:** [Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) evaluators for generative AI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/evaluation-evaluators/rag-evaluators)

Solution: Measure token throughput and mean response latency before and after implementing the proposed change.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Token throughput and average response latency are performance metrics; they do not measure whether a generated response is consistent with the retrieved documents. RAG answer support must be assessed with a groundedness metric that evaluates alignment between the response and its retrieved context without fabricated content.\
\
**Learn more:** [Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Evaluators for Generative AI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/evaluation-evaluators/rag-evaluators)
